statements.paraphrase: Design of the new engine took the best thermal-efficiency point as the steady-state operating point, reached after a quick-start transition.
Best fuel-economy point of the engine stated again, tied to class-leading vehicle fuel economy.
Earlier fixed-point speed of conventional e-POWER was about 2350 rpm; the new engine moves it to 2000 rpm, with roughly 2 dBA less noise.
statements.vehicle: Earlier value: conventional e-POWER (HR12DE 1.2 L NA compact car); new: X-TRAIL

statements.paraphrase: Fixed-point engine speed vs vehicle speed is lower for the SUV than for the 2nd-gen compact over a wide range; speed rises in steps with vehicle speed.
numbers: axis 1000-3000 rpm; step levels roughly 1500-2500 rpm (approx.)
statements.note: reading uncertainty about +-200 rpm; no numeric labels on curves, not for quantitative use

statements.paraphrase: Existing e-POWER is based on fixed-point operation; high compression ratio at the fixed point, low at the output point. Fig. 4 map marks a best-thermal-efficiency point and operating-point-frequency bubbles.

statements.paraphrase: Compared with 2nd-gen compact, the SUV starts fewer times in 20-40 km/h and more in 40-60 km/h; starts reduced at low speed where engine noise exceeds road noise, increased at high speed where it is masked.
statements.vehicle: X-TRAIL (C-seg SUV) vs Compact 1st and 2nd gen
statements.source: text; Fig. 6 bar chart read visually (0-20 SUV slightly above 2nd gen; 60-80 about equal to 2nd gen)
statements.note: bars unlabelled, no counts; qualitative only

statements.paraphrase: At low speed the engine is run as little as possible depending on SOC; at high speed power is actively generated because wind noise masks it.
Engine start/stop depends on vehicle speed, battery SOC and required driving force; larger charge per generation cycle reduces starts per run.
Starts minimized at low speed; control detects road surface and starts the engine when road noise is high.
Road-surface detection starts engine on road noise; earlier e-POWER had to start for brake negative pressure (Fig. 2, urban driving).
Electric control brake removes need to start engine for brake negative pressure; regeneration stops after full charge, avoiding engine speed-up to dissipate energy.
Engine start due to SOC decrease in low-load low-speed case runs at lower speed than before; strong accelerator requests require engine power.

Engine stops at low speed and EV drive uses battery; with high SOC EV drive possible at higher speed. Control keeps EV mode at lowest possible SOC; tuning factors are an upper acceleration limit and permissible SOC.
statements.vehicle: NOTE/SERENA/KICKS lineage (earlier concept, not X-TRAIL specific)

statements.paraphrase: Market data indicates starts can be avoided in normal driving by holding EV mode up to about 0.15 G below about 30 km/h. New concept cut starts at 30 km/h or less by about 70% versus conventional management.
statements.vehicle: Japanese-market NOTE/SERENA/KICKS data (NOT the X-TRAIL e-POWER)
statements.source: text; Fig. 7 histogram axis 0.03-0.18 G, peak near 0.11-0.12 G read visually

statements.paraphrase: Start timing in conventional management set by driver operation, SOC and other offline conditions; road-noise estimation adds a trigger when road noise exceeds engine noise.
When SOC is high EV mode is held as long as possible; when SOC is low the engine starts early to avoid an acceleration drop.

With the turbocharged engine, battery assist is actively used for smooth strong acceleration; assist is coordinated with rising boost pressure to hide turbo lag, while the rate of engine revolution increase is limited for linear sound.
statements.vehicle: X-TRAIL e-POWER with VC-TURBO (first e-POWER with turbo)

statements.paraphrase: Warns that mis-set acceleration limit or SOC can deplete battery-assisted power during acceleration.
Comparison engine with C/R 10.5 needs max output at 5600 rpm to avoid knock (generic comparator); VC-TURBO is 1200 rpm lower and about 3.5 dBA quieter.
statements.vehicle: Generic comparative engine, not the product
